user_prompt: What is the effect of a HIGHER blood pressure target (systolic/diastolic approximately 150-160/95-100 mmHg) compared with a LOWER blood pressure target (approximately 140/90 mmHg) on all-cause mortality in older adults with hypertension? The "higher BP target" arm is the treatment/intervention arm, and the "lower BP target" arm is the control/comparator arm — match this exact framing to whichever arm each trial itself labels as its higher vs lower treatment-target group; do not assume "higher target" means "more/stronger treatment," since it is actually the LESS intensively treated arm in these trials. The single target outcome is ALL-CAUSE MORTALITY (death from any cause) — not cardiovascular mortality, non-cardiovascular mortality, stroke, or any other outcome in this review, which are separate analyses. This is dichotomous (event/no-event) data — please pool it as a Risk Ratio (RR), matching how this outcome is conventionally analyzed in this literature, using each trial's reported number of deaths and total randomized per arm.
